region.text: Courland and Semigallia, the duchy's land of the 1734-1771 shape

events.note: Restores the duchy's land, which is nobody's land in 1750-1759: the duchy holds 4 of its 122 cells. russian-empire ledger/1 (1721, Nystad) took 113 of its cells (compiled draft p1720-p1729), Russia held all 122 on 1 January 1730 (anchor p1730) and nobody holds them on 1 January 1740 (anchor p1740); the duchy's own ledger has no loss. The page infobox: 'Vassal state of Grand Duchy of Lithuania (1561-1569) and Poland-Lithuania (1569-1795)'; it describes no change of the duchy's borders between 1700 and 1795, only the annexation by Russia on 24 October 1795. The vassal tint comes from hierarchy.csv.

region.text: left-bank Ukraine including Kyiv, the Hetmanate of 1686-1764 (the dossier's keyframe cossack-hetmanate_1686)

events.note: Restores the Hetmanate's land, which is Russian direct land in 1750-1759: russian-empire ledger/1 (1721) took 342 of the keyframe's 411 cells and the Hetmanate holds 17. The page: 'The Hetmanate existed between 1648 and 1764' and 'the Hetmanate continued to exist only on the left bank of the Dnieper'; its infobox gives the left bank 208,000 km2 for 1686-1764. The Hetman's post was abolished in 1764 (ledger/19 dissolves the state then).

region.text: left-bank Ukraine including Kyiv, the Hetmanate of 1686-1764

events.note: The page infobox status line: 'After 1654: Protectorate of the Tsardom of Moscow and Russian Empire, concurrent with the Kiev Governorate (1708-1764)'. The Hetmanate has no row under Russia in hierarchy.csv for 1686-1764, so its relation is opened here; the dissolve of 1764 closes it.

region.text: Harar and its plateau, the core of the Emirate without the outer ring of the 150 km disk

events.note: Restores the Emirate's core, which is nobody's land from 1700 to 1875: ledger/1 (1700, 'the outer lands of the Emirate') carries the same region as the whole keyframe, so the Emirate holds 0 of its 316 cells in 1750-1759. The page infobox: 'Sovereign kingdom (1647-1875)'; the Oromo and Somali clans 'gradually annexed' land in the 18th century while paying tax to the Emirate, and the Oromo 'slowly penetrated even the lands held by the Harari, a short distance from the town' (late 18th century). The outer ring stays lost; only the 142-cell Harar region is restored.

The Russian campaign of 1757 ends without a hold on the province: after Gross-Jaegersdorf (30 August 1757) 'the Russians were not yet able to take Konigsberg after using up their supplies of cannonballs at Memel' and Gross-Jaegersdorf and 'retreated soon afterwards'; the occupation begins in January 1758 (next event). Ends the contest of kingdom-of-prussia ledger/15, which otherwise runs to 5 May 1762 (ledger/17). [Reviewer: month 12 changed to 9; the page dates the retreat 'soon afterwards' after the battle of 30 August, not December.]

'In January 1758, the Russians invaded East Prussia'; 'East Prussia had been occupied by Russian forces over the winter and would remain under their control until 1762.' The dossier's own occupation_start is dated 1762 (ledger/16); the occupation ends on 5 May 1762 (ledger/17).

region.text: Sukkertoppen at its first site, present-day Kangaamiut (65 49 30 N, 53 20 15 W), founded 1755

events.note: Replaces the Sukkertoppen part of greenland ledger/9, which the compile skips because the gazetteer has no 'Saqqaq' (Ritenbenck). Colonial Greenland lists 'Ritenbenck and Egedesminde and Sukkertoppen (1755)'; the Kangaamiut page: the settlement was first founded in 1755 on the site of present-day Kangaamiut and 'moved to its present location at Maniitsoq in 1782', so the 1755 colony is drawn at Kangaamiut with the dossier's 40 km disk. [Reviewer: the window agent drew Sukkertoppen at Maniitsoq and Egedesminde at Aasiaat. Egedesminde is dropped: the Aasiaat page has it 'founded in 1759 by Niels Egede', 'north of Nordre Stromfjord', '125 km south of Aasiaat's current location', moved to its current site in 1763; an Aasiaat disk in 1755 is wrong in year and place and the greenland_1757 keyframe would remove it again in 1757. Ritenbenck is not drawn (no place in the gazetteer).]

correction.text: the 1752-1756 shape without Hami (lost in 1696) and without the Tarim Basin, where the Aq Taghliq (Afaqi) Khojas rebelled in Yarkand; Dzungaria and the Ili country in the last year, held by the last resistance

keyframe_overrides.why: The 1757 shape still holds the Tarim Basin, which snaps 3,388 cells back to the Dzungars and then gives them to the Qing in 1757. The page: 'When Amursana rebelled against the Qing dynasty, the Aq Taghliq ... Khojas Burhanuddin and Jahan rebelled in Yarkand'; 'In February 1758, the Qing sent Yaerhashan and Zhao Hui with 10,000 troops against the Aq Taghliq regime'; 'Zhao Hui was besieged by enemy forces at Yarkand until January 1759'; 'The Tarim Basin was pacified in 1759.' So the Tarim Basin is not Qing land in 1757-1758 (qing-dynasty_1757 already leaves it out and qing-dynasty ledger/44 gains it in 1759); this matches the dossier's own ledger/23 loss of the Tarim to the Khojas in 1757.
